title: [ScriptLanguage] Implement Notifications for Script Unload / Reload

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa6c3292-4280-4b5d-a5ca-68ac369456c3


This PR adds two notifications to the script reload pipeline, emitted for every affected script:

1. `Object::NOTIFICATION_BEFORE_UNLOAD_SCRIPT` sent before unload begins.
2. `Object::NOTIFICATION_AFTER_LOAD_SCRIPT` sent after reload is fully finished.

These notifications are designed to provide an officially supported lifecycle boundary around script reloading.

### Why this is needed

#### Better plugin iteration workflow:

For plugin developers, these notifications make hot iteration significantly smoother.  
Plugins can listen for the reload boundary and manually handle unload/reload logic in plugin scripts (for example, when UI is rebuilt in `_enter_tree`), without requiring users to open Project Settings just to toggle a plugin off and on to reload; ideally the extension developer only need to press save to see the plugin updates in for GDScript, and only need to additionally press build for C#.
This improves iteration speed and reduces friction during development.

#### Proper C# reload completion signalling:

For C# developers, this is especially important because there is currently no proper, supported way to know when assembly reload is truly complete.

A commonly mentioned workaround is the undocumented `ISerializationListener`, but it is explicitly discouraged and not officially supported. In addition, `OnBeforeSerialize` / `OnAfterDeserialize` are not invoked at a safe global boundary: while one script receives `OnAfterDeserialize`, other script instances may still be in an invalid transitional state.

By contrast, this PR guarantees that:

- all affected scripts are notified **before** any script state unload starts, and
- all affected scripts are notified **after** all script states have been restored.

This gives developers a deterministic and safe synchronization point for reload-sensitive logic and offers a proper solution for users using the undocumented `ISerializationListener`.

---

**Disclaimer:** The **Commit Message** was generated with assistance from GPT-5.3 Codex. However, I want to emphasize that 100% of the code contributed in this PR is hand-written by a human, with no AI coding plugins or models involved in the coding process.

The original prompt for the commit message:

<details>

```
This Godot Engine branch contains a work-in-progress feature that's pending a Pull Request message. You may check the changes using the corresponding commands against the main branch. Your task is to write a git message for this pr, you need to mention the following:
1. The two additive notifications are triggered for every affected script before unload happens and after reload finishes.
2. These two notifications serve two purposes:
  a. For plugin developers, this is useful as it allows the developer to check for the notification and manually call unload and reload in their plugin script (e.g., when the developer builds every plugin ui in the _enter_tree) without the need for opening the project settings to reload the plugin, effectively improve the iteration speed (all they need to do is press save for GDScript and press build for C# Script to see the plugin gets updated).
  b. For C# developers, this is extra important, as there is currently *NO* way for the developer to properly get notified when the C# assembly reload finishes, in fact, there is, which is the undocumented `ISerializationListener`, however this interface is explicitly unadviced as it's not officially supported, and the `OnBeforeSerialize` and `OnAfterDeserialize` are not been called at the right time: Other script instances maybe are in an invalid state while one of the script has OnAfterDeserialize invoked, in contrast, the notification this PR provides gaurentees *ALL* affected scripts are notified *BEFORE* we start unloading states from scripts and *AFTER* all scripts have their state restored.
```

</details>
